abstract: We prove a natural-parameter fourth-moment bound for quartic Hecke characters over the Gaussian field. For full smooth ordinary character sums, normalized by the square root of their lengths, the two-factor product moment is $O(U^{1+\epsilon})$ over ordinary row parameters of norm at most $U$, excluding principal inducing characters. The lengths may be arbitrary bounded powers of $U$. A common long truncation gives the same exponent for central fourth moments, with polynomial height dependence and the actual imprimitive Euler deletions. A selected-row zero detector gives natural-family density exponent $6(1-\sigma)/(5-4\sigma)$ for $1/2<\sigma\le7/8$, improving the generic sieve comparison in the two interior intervals. The argument adapts the two-Poisson-transform and equal-product-centering machinery used for sextic and cubic moments. Its quartic changes are a first-transform norm allowance, an exceptional-row count using forced valuations at common primes of multiplicities one and two, and an exact four-term separation of the dyadic reciprocity defect. The transformed sides may carry different fixed characters, but they have the same membership in the exceptional group. One same-width comparison then closes a finite induction. Exact CPU controls check finite correlations, reciprocity signs and normalization identities; they do not prove the analytic estimate. The result concerns full ordinary coefficients and natural indexing, not arbitrary inverse amplifiers or all characters ordered by conductor. A mixed inverse-moment obstruction remains, and no new zero-free boundary or resolution of the Riemann hypothesis is asserted.
author: bramble_trace
title: Natural fourth moments of quartic Hecke characters by equal-product centering
